headline: Council voted to move forward with negotiations to acquire right-of-way across the former Long Property for a shared use path.
summary: Members unanimously approved a resolution thanking Tom DePietro for his work on bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure. They also approved the previous meeting's minutes with edits. Discussion covered e-bike ordinance changes, street safety signs, a bike rack survey, and Green Community Festival planning.
decisions: Council voted to move forward with negotiations to acquire right-of-way across the former Long Property for a shared use path, as reported by staff.
Approved a resolution recognizing Tom DePietro's contributions to South Burlington's bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure, unanimously.
Approved the draft minutes of the previous meeting with edits from Bob, by a vote of all in favor.

plain_text:
Page 1 
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee 
August  12, 202 6 
 
The Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee held a regular meeting on August 12, 2026 at 5:30 
pm, in Room 301 of City Hall and by Zoom.  
Committee Members present (R = Remote): Bob Britt (Vice Chair), Kim Maxwell, Donna 
Leban, Freeman Stein and Doug Goodman(R) 
Also present: Erica Quallen Towle (City Staff), Andrew Chalnick (City Council Liaison), Ryan 
Doyle, and Loretta Marriott 
1. Welcome, Emergency Exit and Virtual Meeting Instructions, Gratitude 
a.  Andrew was grateful that the Sewer and Stormwater bond was approved 
overwhelmingly by the voters 
2. Additions, Deletions, or Changes to the Agenda 
a. Freeman asked if we could move up the “Friends for a Walkable/Bikeable 
South Burlington.”  It was decided to move it up to follow the Approval of 
the Minutes. 
b. Ryan was interested in hearing about the Crowdsourcing process to collect 
information on the location of bike racks in the City and where they are 
missing near retail and other locations. 
c. Erica suggested that the Committee hold off this discussion to a later 
meeting so that she had time to have Ariel, the City’s GIS person, design a 
web map that could be used to gather the information.  The fields to include 
were discussed as follows: 
i. Obviously, the location 
ii. Whether anchored to the ground 
iii. How many bikes can be accommodated 
iv. What type/design 
v. Is it covered 
vi. Ability to add a picture 
vii. Then, the location as to where bike racks are missing 
d. Loretta suggested that the Committee recognize with gratitude for all the 
work that Tom DePietro has done for the City and to support bicycle and 
pedestrian infrastructure.  She suggested the following resolution:  
i. “On Tom DiPietro’s departure, the Bicycle & Pedestrian Committee 
recognizes and expresses gratitude for Tom's contributions in
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee – August 12, 2026 | Page 2 
support of South Burlington's Bicycle and Pedestrian Infrastructure. 
We appreciate so many people working together achieving many 
improvements in our active transportation options.  Tom supported 
and believed in this vision. Thank you, Tom.” 
e. Following discussion, the resolution was moved by Donna and seconded by 
Kim, and approved unanimously.  Loretta left the meeting at this point. 
 
3. Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda 
a. None 
4. Consideration of Minutes 
a. Documents: Draft 7/12/2026 Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee Minutes 
b. Bob noted that the first 4 bullets under #7 were duplication from #6 above.  
He also wanted to add that in item 7i that Freeman had also joined the 
Communication subgroup and that the Safe Routes to Schools wording 
should state “group” and not “subgroup. ” He asked for a link to the City 
Update in the agenda  be included in #8.  Finally, that #11biii be changed to 
#11C. 
c. Motion by Freeman to accept edits from Bob and approve. 
d. Seconded by Kim. 
e. Vote: All in favor. Motion Carried 
5. Friends for a Walkable/Bikeable South Burlington Discussion 
a. Bob explained to the new members how his separate entity was formed to 
help advocate for the Penny For Paths initiative back in 2017-2018. 
b. Freeman had been in a Friends of Northampton Trails organization prior to 
moving to Vermont 
c. Freeman and Bob got together to discuss how re-starting the SB Friends 
group could support Bike and Ped initiatives within the City including” 
i. Supporting the DPW with coordinated maintenance like is done with 
Green Up Day 
ii. Safety initiatives 
iii. Education 
iv. Lead Rides 
v. Advocate for the next Penny for Paths tax 
vi. Advocate for more paths and crosswalks 
d. Freeman said that it would ultimately be set up as a 501(c)(3), have awards 
for the best volunteers, hold an annual meeting, etc. 
e. Freeman left the meeting at this time. 
6. City Updates 
a. Erica announced that Chief Breault and City Attorney, Colin McNeil, would 
be presenting E-Bike and E-motto related updates to the City’s ordinances to
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee – August 12, 2026 | Page 3 
City Council on August 18. Erica assured the Committee that its 
recommended ordinance changes were considered in their work.  
Discussion followed that the changes should include financial penalties, 
confiscation and parental responsibility misdemeanor penalties for misuse 
of these devices. 
b. Erica said that the “City Naming Policy” of public assets would also be 
discussed at the August 18th City Council meeting and that the Committee 
could then have the opportunity to provide its recommendation(s). 
c. Erica said that the Council had voted to move forward with negotiations to 
acquire the ROW that crosses the former Long Property that would allow a 
shared use path, etc. to be built to connect the South Village and South 
Pointe neighborhoods. 
d. Weekly updates for the I-89 Bridge project are available by going to the 
“Notify Me” page on the City’s website. 
7. Review Shared Use Path and E-Bike Safety and Education Plan 
a. The Safety and DPW subgroup has moved the safety lawn signs twice with 
about a third of the signs having been absconded. 
b. They submitted a request for reordering the Warn Others When Passing, No 
E-Bikes Over 750W and a request for a new Andy-designed lawn sign that 
dealt with the fact that some users are wearing headphones or earbuds and 
cannot hear approaching runners and bicyclists.  Suggested wording 
included “Look & Listen to Your Surroundings” and “Please be Alert” 
including a graphic showing headphones and earbuds perhaps with a circle 
and a line through them. 
c. The subgroup also asked the City to purchase bike bells to be installed free 
at the upcoming Green Community Festival and other future events where 
bicycles will be present. 
d. Other updates included planned The Other Paper articles, plans for 
permanent signs for next spring, and the need to come up with an school 
education plan. 
8. Road Safety Signage Recommendations – 
https://www.southburlingtonvt.gov/DocumentCenter/View/6103/Street-Signs-
Recommended-to-Improve-Road-Safety---Updated-07-27-2026-PDF  
a. The Safety and DPW subgroup presented its recommendations for Street 
Signs Recommended To Improve Road Safety for Vulnerable Road Users.  
Comments from the Committee on the subgroups draft listing included: 
i. For #1, include a “State Law” plate 
ii. For #3, Erica said the flags needed to be orange instead of red.  She 
said that she would check to see if the City already had the brackets 
needed for the signs.
Bicycle and Pedestrian Committee – August 12, 2026 | Page 4 
iii. For #4, it was recommended that the signs in question be located 
closer to the first crosswalk that someone would come to from each 
City border road entrance. 
iv. For #5, suggested that one be added on Airport Parkway at each end 
of the culvert near the Lime Kiln intersection.  Erica needs to also 
install “Bike Lane Ends” signs.   
v. For #5d, it was recommended that the sign be located on Swift after 
the one makes the turn going north on Spear Street onto Swift. 
vi. For #7, Ryan recommended that if that area were mowed more often 
and the trees and bushes cut back, it would not seem so narrow to 
the rider.  Erica said that the City would remove the “ENDS” sign 
plate if the shoulder were 5 feet wide. 
vii. For #9b, it should read, Dorset Street south of Swift Street 
9. Green Community Festival Planning 
a. Havaleh, Donna and Doug have signed up so far to work the event 
b. The Committee has no bike parking responsibilities 
c. Erica to provide two maps of the active transportation network and of CIP 
projects. 
d. The free bike bell installation needs to be figured out: tools, who, etc. 
e. Erica to provide a large “Respect the Share” code of conduct sign 
f. Have materials present to conduct the bike rack survey 
g. E-moto information – Bob to sent Donna his When is an E-Bike Not an E-
bike article with pictures of illegal e-motos that cannot use paths and 
sidewalks. 
10. Safe Routes to School Group Updates – No meeting held since last Committee 
meeting. 
11. Sub-Group Updates – none except those above 
12. Confirm Next Meeting – September 9th – Bob and Donna will be away, Doug is a 
“solid maybe. ” 
The meeting was adjourned at 7:43pm. 
Bob Britt  - Acting Clerk
